threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: When you ask for a takeaway on Sunday and expect it in under an hour, you might as well be looking for a unicorn. Patience, mate!
Last week on the 59, a lad was trying to impress his mates by showing off a pet snake. People were more scared of missing their stop than the snake.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I realized I was home when the Kebab shop owner knew my order before I spoke—his nod was more welcoming than any ‘hello’.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: In Friedrichshain, it's not uncommon to see people casually eating dinner at 2 AM on a Tuesday, surrounded by laughter and live music from a nearby bar.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can always spot a local—they’ll break into a smile when they hear someone yell ‘¡Cerveza!’ at the taco truck line.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 5-Fulton today and a guy serenaded us with a ukulele. Muni’s the only place you can find a concert while heading to work.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is just all about the plazas, but it’s those hidden bodega corners with locals sipping wine that tell the real story.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their reluctance to try the local al fresco dining and insistence on eating indoors, even in summer.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the Overground is just a trendy name for a regular train. Trust me, it’s a whole vibe—better grab your coffee and accept the delays.
Heard a bloke on the 133 arguing with the driver about the difference between a 'gang' and a 'crew.' Only in Brixton at 2 AM, I tell you.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The morning of the bus strike, I saw a delivery guy on a bike with a whole crate of croissants, navigating the chaos with coffee in one hand and laughter in the other.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a kebab stand that doubles as an art gallery after midnight, showcasing local talent between late-night snacks.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: They know to bring snacks for that BART delay—no tourist is prepared for a meltdown when the train comes to a grinding halt.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a full tuxedo trying to coax his dog off the tracks at Civic Center yesterday. The Muni delays were wild, but this guy? Peak SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is just about trendy cafés. They miss the fact that every plaça has a unique history, like Plaça del Sol's famous night gatherings.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell a newcomer by their bewilderment at the tram schedule. Regulars know it rarely runs on time, but they stand waiting like it’s a Swiss clock.
